examples.en: A prism has a polygon as its base.
A triangular prism and a rectangular prism are both prisms.
We drew a prism in math class.
The side faces of a prism are rectangles.
This box is shaped like a prism.
How are a prism and a cylinder different?

explain: 수학에서 위아래 밑면이 같은 다각형인 기둥 모양 입체도형이에요. 밑면이 동그란 '원기둥', 뾰족한 '각뿔'과 같이 배워요. 일상에서는 '네모난 기둥'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: A triangular prism has triangular bases.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밑면 모양을 앞에 붙여 구체적인 각기둥 이름을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the base shape before the word to name a specific prism.

phrases.en: This box is shaped like a rectangular prism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 네모난 상자처럼 생긴 입체도형을 수학에서 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The math name for a box-like solid with square or rectangular bases.

phrases.en: A prism has two bases.
phrases.nuance_ko: '각기둥의 + 부분 이름'으로 수학 설명을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as 'prism's + part' when explaining the shape in math.

explain_en: In math it is a solid whose top and bottom bases are identical polygons. It is learned alongside the round-based '원기둥' (cylinder) and the pointed '각뿔' (pyramid). In daily life people say things like '네모난 기둥'.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 강둑이 무너질까 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so I'm worried the embankment might collapse.
I run along the riverbank every evening.
The cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the embankment.
Children fly kites on top of the embankment.
It takes ten minutes by bike to get to the embankment.

examples.ko: 강둑은 물이 넘치지 않게 막아 줘요.
examples.en: The embankment keeps the water from overflowing.

explain: 강물이 넘치지 않게 흙이나 돌로 쌓은 둑이에요. 자연스러운 물가인 '강기슭'과 달리 쌓아 올린 언덕이라서, 위에 산책로나 자전거길이 있는 곳이 많아요.

phrases.en: I ride a bike along the river embankment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둑 위의 산책로나 자전거길을 따라 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for moving along the path on top of an embankment.

phrases.en: The villagers built up the river embankment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 흙이나 돌로 만든 둑이라서 '쌓다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since it is made by people from soil or stone, 쌓다 fits well.

phrases.en: There is a bench on top of the embankment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓아 올린 언덕이라서 '위'와 함께 위치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is a raised bank, it pairs with 위 (on top) for location.

explain_en: It is a bank built of earth or stone to keep a river from overflowing. Unlike '강기슭', the natural water's edge, it is a built-up ridge, and many have walking or bike paths on top.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 구김살 없이 밝게 자랐어요.
examples.en: That child grew up bright and carefree.
I smoothed the wrinkles out of my clothes with an iron.
I like her carefree smile.

examples.ko: 빨래를 널 때 구김살을 손으로 털어요.
examples.en: When hanging laundry, I shake out the wrinkles by hand.
Maybe because of worry, his face looked creased and tense.

examples.ko: 구김살 하나 없는 새 교복을 입었어요.
examples.en: I wore a brand-new school uniform without a single wrinkle.

explain: '구김'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만, '구김살 없다'처럼 마음이나 표정이 밝고 어두운 그늘이 없다는 뜻으로 더 자주 써요. 옷의 주름에는 '구김'이 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.example: 구김살 없이 자란 아이라서 누구한테나 친절해요.
phrases.en: He grew up carefree, so he's kind to everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려움이나 그늘 없이 밝고 자유롭게 자란 사람이나 표정을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It praises a person or expression that is bright and free of worry or hardship.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '구김', but it is more often used in '구김살 없다' to describe a bright mind or face with no shadow. For clothes, '구김' sounds more everyday.

en: beside the ear; by the ear

examples.en: The wind brushed past my ear.
That song is still ringing in my ears.
My ear tickled, so I turned around.
Someone whispered softly right by my ear.
I pushed the hair by my ear behind it.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears turned red.

explain: 귀의 바로 옆을 말해요. '귓가에 맴돌다'는 들었던 소리나 말이 계속 들리는 듯한 느낌일 때 자주 써요. 소설이나 노래 가사에서도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: He whispered quietly beside my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀 바로 옆에서 작게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone speaks softly right next to your ear.

phrases.en: The sound of the bell still rings in my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 가까이에서 크게 들리거나 계속 들리는 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sound seems close or keeps echoing.

phrases.en: That voice keeps lingering in my ears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들었던 소리나 말이 끝났는데도 계속 들리는 듯할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sound or words you heard seem to keep playing after they ended.

explain_en: It means the area right beside the ear. '귓가에 맴돌다' is often used when a sound or words you heard still seem to echo. It also appears a lot in novels and song lyrics.

examples.en: When I smile, the corners of my eyes turn down.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 눈꼬리에 선을 길게 그렸어요.
examples.en: When doing makeup, I drew a long line at the outer corner of my eye.
His eyes tilt up at the outer corners, so he looks a bit sharp.
As I got older, wrinkles appeared at the corners of my eyes.
My sibling's eyes droop at the corners, so they look gentle.
A makeup style that lifts the outer corners slightly is in fashion.

explain: 귀 쪽에 가까운 눈의 바깥쪽 끝이에요. 반대로 코 쪽 끝은 '눈머리'라고 해요. '눈꼬리가 올라가다/처지다'로 인상을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My eyes turn up at the corners, so I look sharp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈의 모양으로 인상을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how eye shape affects someone's look.

phrases.en: Her eyes droop at the corners, so she looks gentle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '올라가다'와 반대로 눈 끝이 아래로 내려갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 올라가다; the eye ends point down.

phrases.example: 눈머리는 코 쪽에 있고 눈꼬리는 귀 쪽에 있어요.
phrases.en: The inner corner is near the nose and the outer corner is near the ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈꼬리의 반대쪽, 코 쪽 끝을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The end of the eye near the nose, opposite of 눈꼬리.

explain_en: It is the outer end of the eye, near the ear. The end near the nose is '눈머리'. It is often used to describe someone's look, as in '눈꼬리가 올라가다/처지다'.

examples.en: I iron my shirt every morning.
My mother is ironing the school uniform.
I pressed my suit before the interview.
I burned my hand while ironing.
It has many wrinkles, so I need to iron it.
If you iron slowly, the clothes become neat.

explain: 일상에서는 같은 뜻으로 '다리다'를 많이 써요. '옷을 다리다'가 더 자연스럽고, '다리미질하다'는 일을 하는 동작이라는 느낌이 있어요. '다림질하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I iron my clothes in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다리미질하다'와 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '다리미질하다' and more natural in daily speech.

phrases.en: My father is ironing his pants.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다리미질하다'와 같은 뜻의 다른 표기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An alternative form with the same meaning.

phrases.en: My mom ironed my shirt for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙이면 남을 위해 해 준다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 주다' means doing it for someone else.

explain_en: In daily speech, '다리다' is often used for the same meaning. '옷을 다리다' sounds more natural, while '다리미질하다' feels like naming the chore itself. '다림질하다' is also used.

examples.en: I hung an air freshener in the car.

examples.ko: 방향제 냄새가 너무 강해서 머리가 아파요.
examples.en: The air freshener smell is so strong that I get a headache.

examples.ko: 현관에 놓은 방향제가 벌써 다 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The air freshener I put in the entryway has already run out.
I chose a lemon scent for the bathroom air freshener.
I air out the room by opening a window instead of using an air freshener.
The scent in this air freshener lasts a long time.

explain: 차 안, 현관, 화장실처럼 공간에 좋은 향을 내는 물건이에요. 몸에 뿌리는 '향수'와 다르고, 나쁜 냄새를 없애는 데 초점이 있는 '탈취제'와도 달라요.

phrases.en: I put an air freshener in the bathroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공간에 방향제를 두는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for placing an air freshener in a space.
phrases.en_equiv: to put out an air freshener

phrases.en: The scent got weak, so I changed the air freshener.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 써서 향이 약해졌거나 다른 향을 원할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the scent has faded or you want a different one.

phrases.en: The car smells like air freshener.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 향이든 강한 향이든 방향제의 냄새가 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you smell the air freshener, whether pleasant or strong.

explain_en: It is a product that gives a pleasant scent to a space such as a car, entryway or bathroom. It differs from '향수', which you put on your body, and from '탈취제', which focuses on removing bad smells.

en: to subside; to die down; to wane

examples.en: The flames are gradually dying down.

examples.ko: 그 이야기에 대한 관심이 금세 사그라졌어요.
examples.en: Interest in that story faded quickly.
As time passes, my anger subsides a little.
My fever didn't go down, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 인기가 사그라지기 전에 앨범을 내고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to release an album before my popularity fades.

examples.ko: 소문이 사그라질 때까지 조용히 기다려 보세요.
examples.en: Wait quietly until the rumor dies down.

explain: 불, 열, 화, 관심, 인기처럼 세게 일던 기운이 서서히 약해질 때 써요. '사그라들다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요. 단순히 아래로 내려오는 '가라앉다'보다, 기세가 점점 줄어드는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: The popularity is gradually dying down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사그라지다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 일상에서 둘 다 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 사그라지다, and both are common in daily speech.

phrases.en: As time passed, my anger subsided.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 일던 감정이 서서히 약해질 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when a strong emotion slowly weakens.

phrases.en: The cheering excitement still hasn't died down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기세가 아직 약해지지 않았다고 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form used to say the intensity has not weakened yet.

explain_en: It is used when something that was strong, like fire, fever, anger, interest or popularity, gradually weakens. '사그라들다' is a common variant. Compared with '가라앉다' (settle down), it stresses the force slowly shrinking.

en: to acquire; to learn (a skill, language); to pick up (a found item)

examples.en: Children pick up new languages quickly.
It takes time to acquire this skill.
I acquired Korean while living in Korea.

examples.ko: 길에서 지갑을 습득한 사람은 경찰서에 가져다주세요.
examples.en: If you find a wallet on the street, please take it to the police station.
Acquiring new knowledge is fun.
He picked up driving skills easily.

explain: 언어나 기술은 공부와 경험으로 천천히 몸에 익힐 때 써요. 그리고 '분실물 습득'처럼 잃어버린 물건을 주웠을 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서 기술을 말할 때는 '배우다', '익히다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I found a wallet on the street and reported it as a found item.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 주운 잃어버린 물건을 말해요. 주인이 찾는 물건은 '분실물'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lost item that someone picked up. The owner's side calls it '분실물' (lost item).

phrases.en: I learned the new skill by practicing every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기술이나 지식을 몸에 배게 한다는 뜻으로, 일상에서 '습득하다'보다 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making a skill your own; more natural in daily talk than '습득하다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to master; to get used to

phrases.example: 학교에서 습득한 기술을 일할 때 써요.
phrases.en: I use the skills I acquired at school when I work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배워서 몸에 익힌 기술이나 지식을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to skills or knowledge acquired through learning.

explain_en: For languages and skills, it means gradually making them your own through study and experience. It is also used for finding lost items, as in 분실물 습득. In daily conversation 배우다 or 익히다 sounds more natural for skills.

en: to be frugal; to be thrifty

examples.en: My mother is thrifty and spends household money carefully.

examples.ko: 알뜰한 사람은 세일 기간에 장을 봐요.
examples.en: Thrifty people shop for groceries during the sale period.
I saved my allowance carefully and bought a bag.
My spouse and I manage the household economically.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 알뜰한 가격으로 점심을 팔아요.
examples.en: That shop sells lunch at a good, economical price.
I feel good when I'm told I'm thrifty.

explain: '아끼다'는 쓰는 것을 줄이는 행동이고, '알뜰하다'는 돈이나 물건을 헛되이 쓰지 않고 꼼꼼히 챙기는 사람의 성격에 가까워요. '구두쇠'는 인색하다고 비웃는 말이지만 '알뜰하다'는 칭찬이에요. '알뜰폰'처럼 이름에도 붙어요.

phrases.en: Our family lives frugally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 헛되이 쓰지 않고 생활한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means living without wasting money.

phrases.example: 저는 알뜰하지 않아서 돈이 자주 모자라요.
phrases.en: I'm not thrifty, so I often run out of money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 낭비가 많다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, suggesting you spend a lot.

phrases.en: My friend tends to be thrifty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편이다'를 붙이면 부드럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 편이다 makes the statement softer.

explain_en: '아끼다' is the act of cutting back, while '알뜰하다' describes a person who carefully avoids waste. '구두쇠' mocks someone as stingy, but '알뜰하다' is praise. It also appears in names like '알뜰폰' (budget phone plan).

examples.en: A sweater made of wool is really warm.
In winter I wear wool gloves.

examples.ko: 농부가 봄에 양의 털을 깎아 양털을 모아요.
examples.en: In spring the farmer shears the sheep and collects the wool.

examples.ko: 이 이불은 가벼운데도 양털이 들어 있어서 따뜻해요.
examples.en: This blanket is light, but it has wool inside, so it is warm.

examples.ko: 이 부츠 안쪽에는 양털이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The inside of these boots is lined with wool.
The clouds float fluffily like wool.

explain: '양털'은 양에게서 깎은 털이고, 그 털로 짠 옷감은 '울'이라고도 해요. 옷 상표에는 '울'이라고 적힌 경우가 많아요. '양모'는 같은 말을 한자어로 쓴 것인데 상품 설명 같은 글에서 써요.

phrases.en: If you cover yourself with a wool blanket, it is very warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양털로 만든 물건 앞에 '양털'을 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '양털' before the name of an item made from sheep's wool.

phrases.en: This coat is 100% wool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양털로 짠 옷감을 말하고, 옷 상표에 자주 적혀 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means fabric woven from sheep's wool and often appears on clothing labels.

phrases.en: The farmer shears the sheep's wool in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양에게서 털을 잘라 낼 때 '깎다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '깎다' for cutting the wool off a sheep.

explain_en: 양털 is the hair shorn from a sheep, and fabric made from it is also called 울. Clothing labels often say 울. 양모 is the same thing in a Chinese-character word and appears in product descriptions and similar writing.

examples.ko: 큰따옴표 안의 말을 다시 인용할 때는 작은따옴표를 써요.
examples.en: Use single quotation marks when you quote something inside double quotes.
Inner thoughts are marked with single quotation marks.
The single quotation marks are missing, so the sentence feels awkward.
I emphasized this word by putting it in single quotation marks.
The single quote key is next to Enter on the keyboard.
Newspaper headlines often use single quotation marks.

explain: 큰따옴표는 직접 대화나 인용에 쓰고, 작은따옴표는 속마음, 강조, 인용 안의 인용에 써요. 신문 제목에서는 말을 줄여서 인용할 때도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I put words I want to emphasize in single quotation marks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글에서 따옴표를 쓰는 방법을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when explaining how to use quotation marks in writing.

phrases.en: In writing, dialogue is marked with quotation marks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰따옴표와 작은따옴표를 모두 포함하는 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word covering both double and single quotation marks.

phrases.en: Words someone said directly are written in double quotation marks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은따옴표와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easy to remember when paired with the headword.

explain_en: Double quotation marks are for direct speech or quotes, while single ones are for inner thoughts, emphasis and quotes within quotes. Newspaper headlines also often use them to quote shortened remarks.

examples.en: While reading, I rediscovered the joy of reading.
On the trip, I came to rediscover myself.
I think I've rediscovered how precious family is.

examples.ko: 옛 친구를 만나 서로를 재발견하려고 노력했어요.
examples.en: I met an old friend and we tried to get to know each other anew.

examples.ko: 이번 전시는 한국 그림을 재발견할 좋은 기회예요.
examples.en: This exhibition is a great chance to rediscover Korean painting.

examples.ko: 오래된 동네를 걷다가 숨은 매력을 재발견해요.
examples.en: Walking through an old neighborhood, I rediscover its hidden charm.

explain: 모르던 것을 처음 찾는 '발견하다'와 달리, 알고 있던 것의 좋은 점을 새삼 깨닫는다는 뜻이에요. 사람, 장소, 취미 등에 '~을/를 재발견하다' 형태로 써요.

phrases.en: I came to rediscover my friend whom I met after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계기가 있어서 저절로 새롭게 알게 됐다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests you came to realize it naturally because of some occasion.

phrases.en: I want to try rediscovering my neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한번 시도해 본다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the sense of giving it a try.

phrases.en: I came to see my friend in a new light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좀 더 쉬운 말로, 사람을 새롭게 좋게 볼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler expression, often used when you start seeing a person in a better light.
phrases.en_equiv: to see in a new light

explain_en: Unlike '발견하다' (to find something unknown), it means to newly realize the good in something you already knew. It is used with people, places and hobbies as '~을/를 재발견하다'.

en: to develop; to unfold; to launch (a campaign)

examples.en: The company is rolling out a new ad campaign.
The teacher developed the story in an interesting way.

examples.ko: 시민들이 환경 보호 운동을 전개하고 있어요.
examples.en: Citizens are carrying out an environmental protection campaign.
Order matters when you develop an argument.

examples.ko: 작가가 사건을 빠르게 전개해서 지루하지 않아요.
examples.en: The writer moves the events along quickly, so it isn't boring.
Please tell me how to develop a piece of writing.

explain: '전개하다'는 이야기, 주장, 운동처럼 시작해서 점점 이어 가는 일에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '하다', '벌이다'가 비슷하게 쓰이고, 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 나와요. 명사 '전개'는 '이야기 전개가 빠르다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The school is running an environmental campaign.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 참여하는 운동을 펼친다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means carrying out an effort that many people join.

phrases.en: He developed his argument in the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 생각을 차례대로 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you present your ideas step by step.

phrases.en: We carry on the work according to the plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 이야기를 계속 이어 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means continuing a task or story step by step.

explain_en: 전개하다 is used for stories, arguments or campaigns that start and then keep developing. In daily talk, 하다 or 벌이다 can fill a similar role, and 전개하다 appears more in writing and presentations. The noun 전개 is used like '이야기 전개가 빠르다'.

dis.h: launch or develop a campaign, argument

p.n: 진행하다 just means carrying it on, without the sense of expanding or launching it.

examples.en: In the old days, people made roofs out of straw.
The farmer piled up the straw.
Once straw gets wet, it doesn't dry easily.
Grandmother wrapped the eggs in straw and gave them to me.
It's a country village that smells of straw.
Even straw rots when it gets old.

explain: 짚은 벼 같은 곡식을 거두고 남은 마른 줄기라서 지붕·신발·새끼줄 같은 시골 물건에 쓰였어요. '짚신', '짚단'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙을 때가 많고, '지푸라기'는 짚의 작은 조각을 말해요.

phrases.en: The farmer tied up a bundle of straw.
phrases.nuance_ko: '짚'을 묶어 놓은 한 덩이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A tied-up bundle of straw.

phrases.en: People in the old days wore straw sandals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짚으로 만든 옛날 신발이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Old-style shoes made of straw.

phrases.en: There is a piece of straw stuck in your hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짚의 작은 조각 하나를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small piece of straw.

explain_en: 짚 is the dry stalk left after harvesting rice or other grain, so it was used for country items such as roofs, shoes, and rope. It often attaches before another word, as in '짚신' (straw sandals) and '짚단' (straw bundle), and '지푸라기' is a small piece of straw.

en: to be sparkling; to be shining; to be gleaming

examples.en: The child's eyes are so bright that they're adorable.
After a good sleep, my mind is wide awake.
I looked at the teacher with bright eyes.
All the students' eyes are so bright.
The night sky with sparkling stars is pretty.

examples.ko: 커피를 마셨더니 눈이 초롱초롱해서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: After coffee my eyes are wide open and I can't sleep.

explain: 눈이 맑고 또렷할 때, 그리고 졸리지 않고 정신이 또렷할 때도 써요. 밤하늘의 별에도 쓸 수 있어요. 눈이 흐릿한 느낌의 '흐리멍덩하다'와 반대 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: She reads the storybook with bright, clear eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형으로, 눈을 설명할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, most often used to describe eyes.

phrases.en: My eyes were really bright when I was little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, for describing how someone used to look.

phrases.en: I'm sleepy, so my eyes aren't bright.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 졸리거나 피곤한 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, for sleepy or tired states.

explain_en: It describes eyes that are clear and bright, and also a mind that is awake and not sleepy. It can be used for stars in the night sky too. It feels opposite to '흐리멍덩하다', which means dull and hazy.

en: fashion industry; the world of fashion

examples.en: That designer is very famous in the fashion world.
Trends change fast in the fashion world.
My dream is to work in the fashion industry.
This season's talk of the fashion world is jeans.

examples.ko: 패션계 사람들은 옷을 정말 잘 입어요.
examples.en: People in the fashion industry dress really well.
Even the overseas fashion world is paying attention to Korean designers.

explain: '-계'는 '연예계, 정치계, 의료계'처럼 어떤 분야의 사람들과 세계를 가리켜요. '패션 업계'는 회사와 산업 쪽, '패션계'는 디자이너·모델까지 포함한 분야 전체 느낌이에요. 보통 '패션계에서 일하다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 패션 업계는 새 시즌을 미리 준비해요.
phrases.en: The fashion industry prepares for new seasons in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사와 산업 쪽에 더 가까운 말이에요. '패션계'와 비슷하지만 경제 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Closer to companies and the industry. It is similar to '패션계' but sounds more business-oriented.

phrases.en: My older sister wants to work in the fashion world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 분야에서 직업을 갖는다는 뜻이에요. 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means having a career in that field. The most common collocation.
phrases.en_equiv: to work in the fashion world

phrases.en: All the people from the fashion world gathered at the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 디자이너, 모델 같은 사람들을 함께 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to designers, models, and others together.

explain_en: The suffix '-계' means a field and the people in it, as in '연예계, 정치계, 의료계'. '패션 업계' leans toward companies and industry, while '패션계' feels like the whole field including designers and models. You often say '패션계에서 일하다'.

examples.en: There are still tickets left for the down-line train.

examples.ko: 사고 때문에 하행선이 막혀서 도착이 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: The down line was blocked by an accident, so my arrival was delayed.
I'm taking the line going down from Seoul to Busan.

examples.ko: 주말 저녁에는 하행선보다 상행선이 더 막혀요.
examples.en: On weekend evenings the up line is more jammed than the down line.
The platform for the down line is on the second basement level.

examples.ko: 고장 때문에 하행선 열차가 잠시 멈췄어요.
examples.en: Because of a breakdown, the down-line train stopped for a while.

explain: 기차나 고속도로에서 서울에서 먼 지방 쪽으로 내려가는 노선을 말해요. 반대로 서울로 올라오는 쪽은 '상행선'이에요. 이동 방향을 말할 때 '내려간다/올라간다'고 하는 한국어 습관과 이어져요.

phrases.en: The down-line train arrives in ten minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서울에서 멀어지는 방향으로 가는 기차를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a train heading away from Seoul.

phrases.en: The down line is clear, but the up line is jammed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말로 함께 외워 두면 방향을 말하기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Its opposite; learning them together helps you talk about direction.

phrases.en: The down-bound road is very jammed on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고속도로에서 지방으로 가는 차가 많아 느릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when traffic heading out of Seoul is slow on the highway.

explain_en: On trains and highways it is the route heading away from Seoul toward the provinces. The opposite, toward Seoul, is '상행선'. It matches the Korean habit of saying you go 'down' to the provinces and 'up' to Seoul.

en: to liberate; to set free; to emancipate

examples.en: That leader freed many slaves.

examples.ko: 아이들을 공부에서 해방하고 싶다는 부모가 있어요.
examples.en: Some parents say they want to free their children from studying.
People fought to liberate their country.
Exercise frees my mind from worries.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 사람을 힘든 일에서 해방할 거예요.
examples.en: This machine will free people from hard work.

examples.ko: 군대가 마을을 해방하면서 사람들이 거리로 나왔어요.
examples.en: As the army liberated the town, people came out into the streets.

explain: 억압이나 속박에서 풀어 줄 때 써요. 풀려나는 쪽은 '해방되다'를 써요. 한국에서는 1945년에 일제강점기가 끝난 일을 '해방'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The slaves were finally liberated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해방하다'는 풀어 주는 쪽이 주어이고, '해방되다'는 풀려나는 쪽이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '해방하다' has the one who frees as subject; '해방되다' has the one who is freed.

phrases.example: 그 법이 아이들을 힘든 일에서 해방시켰어요.
phrases.en: That law freed children from hard labor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해방하다'와 뜻이 같고, 누군가를 어떤 일에서 벗어나게 한다는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '해방하다'; it stresses making someone break free from something.

phrases.example: 새장 문을 열고 새를 풀어 줬어요.
phrases.en: I opened the cage and let the bird go.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬운 말로 가둔 것을 놓아 줄 때 일상 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain everyday phrase for letting go of something that was held or confined.

explain_en: It means releasing someone from oppression or restraint, while the one who is released uses '해방되다'. In Korea, the end of Japanese colonial rule in 1945 is called '해방'.
